checks.detail: Actual response, preserved raw, frozen source package, visible search evidence and accepted analysis context independently SHA-256 verified. Trimmed extracted soul field matches capture field hash; removing only the completion marker reproduces the body.
All nine unique Markdown source URLs actually opened and their relevant passages read; supplementary volume six resolves the combined-volume link label.
Full actual manuscript read with the seven required headings in order: 說話邏輯、壓力反應、核心驅動、慣性盲點、情感結構、參照系、內在裂縫. Sections use concrete individual events and culminate in the father/ruler conflict.

1687 demand for candid ministerial advice and 1708 undisclosed heir decision / exclusive final裁奪 are explicit in the cited annal and edicts. The synthesis is marked inference rather than invented dialogue.

1669 handling and clemency match the biography. 1690 illness is correctly distinguished from the 1696 personal middle-route command; western army and actual battlefield roles remain assigned to Feiyanggu.

1673–1681 war, 1676 Wang Fuchen restoration and 1683 Zheng/Liu surrender honors verified. The interpretation of submission to central order does not falsely assert every rebel was spared or every rival eliminated.

1694 royal criticism of Yu Chenglong’s accusations, actual official sanctions, and 1722 rejection of increased fire-loss levies amid military/corruption deficits match. Institutional insufficiency is the author’s historical interpretation, not a claim that no delegation ever occurred.

Regnal year 26, lunar twelfth-month Tian Tan prayer, requested transfer of lifespan, tears, personal bedside attendance and recollection of childhood care directly appear in volume 131. The author’s attachment inference is anchored in these statements rather than an invented private scene.
1708 Nanyuan hunting, recollection of former outings with the crown prince and other sons, early return in illness and grief, and actual summons / meeting correspond to volume 234.

1675 appointment; 1708 first deposition; 1709 formal restoration; 1712 second deposition retain distinct dates. Volumes 233/234/236 describe the emperor’s contemporary illness / witchcraft explanation; the manuscript expressly attributes it to that official explanation rather than asserting supernatural causation.

Early instruction, Zhang Ying / Xiong Cilu, imperial expectations and threats to dynastic trust are directly recorded. Father-versus-ruler tension and hunting / encirclement analogy remain labelled推斷 or詮釋 and are not treated as literal psychological diagnoses.
